title: Current - voltage characteristics in magnetic field for layered superconductor with intrinsic pinning of Josephson vortices
authors: T. B. Charikova, V. N. Neverov, M. R. Popov, S. D. Popov, N. G. Shelushinina, A. A. Ivanov
abstract: The results of measurements of the transverse voltage in the Hall configuration, Uy, under conditions of motion of the charge and vortex subsystems in orhtogonal magnetic and electric fields on epitaxial films of the layered high-temperature superconductor Nd2-xCexCuO4 are presented. the motion of Josephson vortices across CuO2 layers (along the c-axis) is analyzed considering the effects of intrinsic pinning. An exponential dependence of critical depinning current jc(B) for Josephson vortices is established in contrast to the power law dependences for Abrikosov vortices. With increasing external magnetic field after the depinning by a magnetic field at B=Bc, the onset of the vortex creep regime, which evolves into the flux-flow regime at crossover field B=Bf, is observed.
summary: This paper experimentally measures the current-voltage characteristics of a layered high-temperature superconductor to study Josephson vortex motion. Key findings include establishing an exponential dependence for the critical depinning current and mapping the transition from flux creep to flux flow regimes. This work provides detailed insights into pinning mechanisms crucial for superconducting applications.
main_problem: The study investigates the current-voltage characteristics and vortex dynamics in layered high-temperature superconductors under the influence of intrinsic pinning.
main_result: The critical depinning current for Josephson vortices exhibits an exponential dependence on the magnetic field, contrasting with the power law behavior seen for Abrikosov vortices.
method: Measurements of the transverse voltage ($U_y$) in the Hall configuration were performed on epitaxial films using varying electric and magnetic fields.
model_or_system: The physical system is epitaxial films of the layered superconductor Nd2-xCexCuO4/SrTiO3, focusing on the motion of Josephson vortices across CuO2 layers along the c-axis.
key_observables: Transverse voltage ($U_y$), critical depinning current ($j_{cc}(B)$), magnetoresistance ($R(B)$), and Hall resistance ($R_H(B)$).
important_parameters: Magnetic fields up to 9 T, helium temperatures (1.7 K and 4.2 K), and the crossover field ($B_{ff}$) separating flux creep and flux flow regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the intrinsic pinning mechanism dominates vortex dynamics, and the flux motion can be modeled using thermally activated flux-creep theory.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the current-voltage (j vs U_y) characteristics and the magnetoresistance/Hall resistance dependence on the magnetic field.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the CV characteristics, derives $R(B)$ and $R_H(B)$, models the flux creep regime using empirical fits, and discusses the transition to the flux flow regime.
why_interesting: The study of vortex dynamics and pinning in HTSCs provides a complex, non-equilibrium many-body problem that shares conceptual links with understanding energy dissipation and collective excitations in strongly correlated quantum materials.
